To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The complete amino acid sequence of the rabbit fast skeletal muscle light meromyosins (LM) has been deduced from the nucleotide sequence of cDNA clones.
the complete sequence of the coding region for a rabbit fast skeletal myosin heavy-chain isoform has been determined and that the corresponding gene is part of a multigene locus of 8-11 members.
the class I cDNA clone corresponds to the most abundant form of myosin-heavy-chain mRNA in rabbit fast skeletal muscle and that it codes for the complete light-meromyosin portion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of cDNA clones coding for the light meromyosins of the myosin heavy chains expressed in the rabbit fast skeletal muscle.
the molecular cloning of cDNA coding the complete light meronymosin portion of the myosin heavy-chain polypeptide of rabbit fast skeletal muscle.
a fast skeletal muscle myogen-specific cDNA clone that codes for the complete light chain portion of the myosin heavy-chain molecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this clone represents a member of a family of at least three different myosin heavy-chain genes expressed in fast skeletal rabbit muscle.
the cDNA clone of class I represents the complete light meronyosin portion of the myosin heavy-chain gene of rabbit fast skeletal muscle.
class I clones code for a myosin heavy-chain mRNA that is expressed in fast skeletal muscles of rabbits and that the corresponding gene is present in a multigene-family form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated and sequenced a cDNA clone coding for a fast skeletal muscle myofibril-specific mRNA which corresponds to a multigene myosin heavy-chain family of 8 to 12 members.
we have isolated cDNA clones corresponding to at least two, possibly three, different myosin heavy chains expressed in rabbit fast skeletal muscle.
there are at least 3 classes of myosin-heavy-chain cDNAs in the library, each of which is represented by 8-12 different genes in the rabbit genome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the myosin heavy-chain gene family and have determined that the gene for a fast skeletal muscle myofibrillar protein has a large number of members.
the myosin heavy-chain gene family is larger than expected.
the light meromyosins of rabbit and human fast skeletal muscle myo-sins are more homologous to each other than to the light meromy-sins of the slow skeletal muscle isoforms of the two species.
